name: Trip to Hillwood Estate, Museum & Gardens
description:
Join CEAd Jorge and CC Kelvin for a trip to Hillwood Estate, Museum & Gardens in honor of Women's History Month!

RSVP Required due to limited number of tickets!

 

What is Hillwood?

Hillwood Estate, Museum & Gardens is the former home of Marjorie Merriweather Post (more below!). Hillwood is known for its large decorative French and Russian art. It houses one of the most comprehensive collections of Russian imperial art outside of Russia, a distinguished collection of French art from the 1700s, twenty-five acres of landscaped gardens and natural woodlands, and one of America's finest orchid collections (which will be blooming throughout March!).

 

Who was Marjorie Merriweather Post?

Marjorie Merriweather Post (1887 - 1973) was a businesswoman, philanthropist, socialite, heiress of the Postum Cereal Company, and alumna of the Mount Vernon Seminary (now GW's Mount Vernon Campus). As the heiress to the Postum Cereal Company, later General Foods, Marjorie Post was among the wealthiest women of her time. She exerted a strong hand in the business affairs of her company long before women appeared in major corporate boardrooms. Post also dedicated her intense focus to collecting French and Russian art as well as to making significant charitable contributions throughout her life, supporting organizations such as the Boy Scouts of America and the Mount Vernon Seminary.

name: DC Art All Night: U Street Saturday
description:
https://districtbridges.org/events/art-all-night-u-street/



Art All Night is a vibrant citywide celebration of the performing and visual arts in Washington, D.C. This year, the event will take place on September 12 and 13, 2025. The festival showcases a diverse range of local talent and creativity, highlighting the intersection of art and business across various commercial corridors.

The event features a wide array of activities, including painting, photography, sculpture, crafts, fashion, music, dance, theater, film, and poetry. Both indoor and outdoor venues, such as public spaces, local businesses, and restaurants, will host these activations. Each participating neighborhood plays a role in corridor revitalization by activating public spaces, highlighting local artists, attracting new visitors, and driving increased sales for small and local businesses. 

On Saturday, September 13th we invite you to join us in celebration of the performing and visual arts up and down the U Street Corridor in Washington, D.C.

U Street Corridor or Greater U Street, sometimes known as Cardozo/Shaw, is a neighborhood in Washington, D.C., located in Northwest D.C. Centered along U Street, the neighborhood is one of Washington's most popular nightlife and entertainment districts, as well as one of the most significant African American heritage districts in the country. The area was largely built after the U.S. Civil War and with the arrival of the Washington streetcar system in the 1880s, the neighborhood development boomed. By 1920, the neighborhood was predominantly African-American and flourished as the "Black Broadway", the heart of African-American culture in Washington.

Students should plan to meet Dr. Dwayne Kwaysee Wright (FiR in Guthridge Hall) @7pm in the Guthridge Hall Lobby @7pm.

name: GWU Death Penalty Action Awareness Event
description: The GWU Death Penalty Action, with the help of the national Death Penalty Action, will be hosting a death penalty awareness event open to the public. We will have representatives from the GW Law School, American University, and more, pending approval. This event will feature a travelling photography exhbit, featuring personal and raw images related to the death penalty, and several speakers with first-hand perspectives on the death penalty with a Q+A session. We will also have several stations with different representatives (Law School, International Reps.) who will have informational resources to give out and who will answer questions from attendees. Additionally, this event will have a "Take Action" station, where attendees can access petitions, protest dates, and student advocates to help inform them about how they can practice advocacy themselves. The event will have free food and merchandise, as well.

name: New Member Retreat
description:
Welcome to Fraternity and Sorority Life at GW! If you’ve recently joined a fraternity or sorority, the New Member Retreat is your next step—and it’s required.

This full-day experience is your opportunity to dive deeper into what it truly means to be part of the fraternity and sorority community. You’ll explore the national and local history of these organizations, understand the values that continue to shape Greek Life today, and have honest conversations about hazing prevention and outdated traditions that no longer reflect who we are.

Led by the Office of Fraternity and Sorority Life, this retreat is also a chance to connect with new members from other chapters and councils, share your experiences, and start building a more inclusive, supportive community.

Check-in begins at 9:00 AM, and you must attend the full event to receive credit—so mark your calendar, bring your energy, and get ready to grow.
